# Processing Toolbox — Milestone 3 (M13.3) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Finish the processing toolbox: the two `three_d` solids tools (§7.2 Measure solids, §7.3 Validate solids), the three `spatial` cross-layer tools (§7.5 Join attributes by location, §7.6 Aggregate buildings per area, §7.7 Distance to nearest), the **New layer** destination (§6 OUTPUT and "What a derived layer is", §8 persistence, scenarios 10-12) for every implemented tool, and the four groups M2 carried forward — engine-death hardening off the table FIFO, Style-by-result palette rotation and its Color-by-at-Save fix, and the M1/M2 leftovers (write-step SQL in the log, scroll-into-view, the synthetic-vs-computed roof-area explanation, a version-aware streaming-table sweep).

**Architecture:** Seven strands, in this order, each landing before its consumers. (1) A real-engine probe suite pins every `three_d` and `spatial` fact this plan's SQL rests on, under the same node harness M1 and M2 used. (2) The plugin submodule tags each `Surface` with the CityJSON geometry TYPE it came from, which is what makes "has a SOLID at LoD X" answerable from tags alone — M2's "nothing walks a whole layer's geometry synchronously" still binds. (3) Three shared seams the tools need: typed output columns on the definition, a **"Reading source"** phase that re-registers a reader-backed layer's bytes (the door `export.ts` already uses), and a `styleByResult` descriptor so the result card has ONE branch instead of five. (4) The solids tools, each a params module → executor → PARAMETERS section → the single commit that flips `implemented` and extends `useLodOptions`. (5) The cross-layer machinery: the run queue learns a SOURCE layer and a VECTOR target, the vector layer is reprojected app-side with proj4 and registered as a per-run `__src_<runId>` table dropped in a `finally`, the building proxy becomes one SQL builder, and the three tools follow. (6) The New-layer destination: a derived layer's model copy, its table and its layer row are prepared inside the run's own FIFO slot and published together as the last step, exactly as §6.1's cancel boundary requires. (7) The carried hardening and the leftovers.

**Tech Stack:** DuckDB-wasm 1.33.1-dev64.0 (DuckDB 1.5.5, `wasm_eh`) with `cityjson` v0.4.0, `three_d` v0.2.0 and core `spatial`, reached only through `src/insights/duckdb.ts`; proj4 for app-side reprojection; React 19 + Zustand; Vitest + @testing-library/react (jsdom) for units, `DUCKDB_INTEGRATION=1` node probes for engine facts, `agent-browser` + Playwright Chromium for the gate smoke; plugin submodule `@cityjson/navara-core` (pnpm).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-processing-toolbox-design.md` — §2 (engine facts), §3 (vocabulary: target, source, scope, destination), §6 (TARGET, LoD, PARAMETERS validation, OUTPUT incl. "Write to → New layer", "What a derived layer is", extension and workload notes), §6.1 (phases, frozen parameters, the publication step), §6.2 (the done card, both destinations, Style by result, Undo), §6.3, §6.4 (the log as a reproducible record), §7 (common rules, contributors, roll-ups), §7.2-§7.7, §8 (where results appear, persistence), §9 (what stays out), §10 scenarios 2, 3, 5, 8, 10, 11, 12. Read it before any task.

**Predecessor:** `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-11-processing-toolbox-m2.md` and its committed ledger `docs/superpowers/handoffs/2026-09-12-processing-toolbox-m2/sdd/progress.md`. Every "Ruling:" line in that ledger binds; nothing here re-litigates one. M2's own Global Constraints are repeated below because they all still apply.

## Global Constraints

Carried from M1 and M2 (unchanged, and every one still applies):

- Never run bare `vite`/`vp dev`/`vp build`; use `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, `npx vp check`, `npx vitest run`, `npx tsc -b --noEmit`. `.env` is dotenvx-encrypted.
- `src/insights/duckdb.ts` is the ONLY importer of `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm`. **Every NEW export from `duckdb.ts` must be added to all 32 `vi.mock(".../insights/duckdb", …)` factories**, and every new export from `layerTables.ts` to all 6 `vi.mock(".../insights/layerTables", …)` factories (counts verified on `develop` @ `55e4e00`). **Both counts are the BASELINE, not a constant**: a task that authors a new suite mocking either module raises its count, and the sweeping task greps rather than trusting the number (Task 11 adds a seventh `layerTables` factory, which Task 21's sweep therefore covers). The task that adds an export lists the files and does the sweep in its own commit. A task that adds a FIELD to an exported TYPE sweeps something else — the hand-built literals of that type — and says so: Task 5 sweeps the 16 `LayerTable` literals, Task 21 sweeps the 12 `Layer` literals AND adds two `layerTables` exports to the 6 factories.
- Test files import from `"vitest"`, never `"vite-plus/test"`. Vitest runs under Node 24: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims:$PATH"`. The full suite runs in the BACKGROUND to a file, never in the foreground.
- `npx vp check` baseline is **0 errors / 56 warnings**. A task that adds a warning fixes it before review; the baseline is a gate.
- Submodule-first: commit inside `packages/cityjson-navara-plugins`, push it (`git -C packages/cityjson-navara-plugins push origin main`), then the pointer bump plus parent-side fixture fixes in the parent. Always `cd` into the submodule for pnpm; never `pnpm -C`. `pnpm install` again after any app-side `npm install`.
- Commits: small, one change each, prefixed `feat:` / `fix:` / `test:` / `docs:` / `refactor:` / `chore:`; directly on `develop`. **No attribution trailers of any kind** (the harness's `Claude-Session:` line included).
- UI: Soft Utility tokens from `src/app/flatControls.css` (`--control-radius` 8px, `--control-height` 38px, `--control-height-compact` 30px, `--processing-caption` 84px). Verify new controls against peers in a real browser.
- Copy: every user-visible string is verbatim from the spec, or one of the seventeen **[adapted copy]** strings the repo owner ACCEPTED at the plan gate (the table under "Copy table", and "Decisions recorded (2026-09-12)" items 2, 3 and 5). Every one is settled; no task invents a string, reopens one as a question, or gates work on an answer.
- Features, not rows (§7): a BuildingPart never counts as a building; roll-ups are per feature (`COALESCE("feature_id","id")`); the Style-by-result median is over root rows (`buildMedianSql`, `sql.ts:438-439`).
- `!implemented` outranks every eligibility reason (`eligibility.ts:44`). A tool flips to `implemented: true` in the SAME commit that extends `useLodOptions` for it (M2 ledger, Task 11 concern) and only after its executor, LoD answer and parameters exist.
- No unimplemented tool may claim a fact about the user's data: `implemented === false` renders no LoD control, no column list and no geometry verdict.
- Nothing walks a whole layer's geometry synchronously. LoD eligibility and counts read surface TAGS only and call no metric function; a run measures only the scoped features' contributors, in batches that yield to the event loop.
- `ensureExtension` runs INSIDE `runOnTableQueue` as the `"extension"` run phase, so a first `spatial` load blocks table builds for its ~24 MB download, once per session. Accepted deliberately (architecture note, M13.2).
- `ensureExtension` is not abortable; every call site checks `signal.aborted` after it resolves.
- `raced(promise, signal | null)` / `racedWithDeath(promise)` in `src/insights/engineAwait.ts` is the ONE abort+death race. Nothing writes a second copy of it.
- Pre-commit runs `vp staged`; pre-push runs `vp check`, `tsc -b --noEmit`, `vp test run`. Do not bypass the hooks.
- Implementers locate edit sites by the QUOTED code, never by this plan's line numbers (M2 ledger ruling; two milestones' worth of drift is expected).
- `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is on: every indexed read is `T | undefined` and must be narrowed.

New in M3:

- **`ST_3DTryFromWKB`, never `ST_3DFromWKB`.** `ST_3DFromWKB` RAISES "Unsupported WKB geometry type for SOLID_3D import: type code 1006" on a MultiPolygon Z, and one such row fails the whole statement. `ST_3DTryFromWKB` returns NULL instead.
- **`ST_3DVolume` only under `is_valid`.** It RAISES "ST_3DVolume: solid is not closed" on a parsed-but-unclosed solid, and one such row fails the whole statement. The only guarded shape is `CASE WHEN r.is_valid THEN ST_3DVolume(s) END` where `r = ST_3DValidationReport(s)`. Every other `three_d` measure is safe on an invalid solid.
- **There is no `ST_3DIsValid`.** Validity is `ST_3DValidationReport(s).is_valid`.
- **`spatial` footprints come from LoD 0 columns only.** `ST_GeomFromWKB` RAISES "Unsupported geometry type in WKB" on a PolyhedralSurface Z (every solid LoD). A footprint proxy is offered only where the target has an LoD 0 geometry column AND a reader.
- **Reprojection is app-side with proj4. `ST_Transform` is never called**, even though it exists in the wasm build (spec §2's decision, and it keeps the vector path identical whether or not `spatial` ships PROJ data).
- **The per-run vector table is `__src_<runId>`**, created in the `"source"` phase and dropped in a `finally` that runs on every exit path (done, failed, cancelled, engine death). A vector layer's durable copy is its feature `properties`, never a table.
- **Nothing new is persisted.** Snapshot schema stays v4; a derived layer is OMITTED from the snapshot (§8) and the active-layer index and layer order are written as if it were not there.
- **The FCB attribute write-back stays OUT** (repo owner, 2026-09-11, "future consideration"), including where the New-layer and vector-results work touches Details. A streaming run's values still live in the table only.
- **Out of scope, and no task may add them** (§9): footprint operations to a new layer, the field calculator, city-to-city joins, replay of runs on restore, computing on layers without a reader.

## Facts about the current code and the real engine (verified 2026-09-12 on `develop` @ `55e4e00`)

Every file:line below was read on this checkout. Treat a citation that does not match as a cue to re-read, never as a licence to improvise.

### What real DuckDB 1.5.5 does with `three_d` (probed 2026-09-12, node bindings, the same wasm build the app ships)

- `INSTALL three_d FROM community; LOAD three_d;` works (v0.2.0, `679ee09`, ~0.2 s). `INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;` works (`eb1e57c`, ~1 s when cached). `ensureExtension(name)` (`duckdb.ts:540`) is the browser door; the node harness (`tests/integration/duckdb/harness.ts:88`, `openDuckDB`) can issue the same statements, so a real-engine probe suite for both is possible — Task 1.
- Function names, exact: `ST_3DTryFromWKB(blob) → SOLID_3D or NULL`, `ST_3DFromWKB` (**never use**, see Global Constraints), `ST_3DVolume`, `ST_3DSurfaceArea`, `ST_3DArea` (same value as `ST_3DSurfaceArea` on these fixtures), `ST_3DFootprintArea`, `ST_3DZMin`, `ST_3DZMax`, `ST_3DBounds → STRUCT(min_x, min_y, min_z, max_x, max_y, max_z)`, `ST_3DIsClosed`, `ST_3DIsManifold`, `ST_3DIsOriented`, `ST_3DNumShells`, `ST_3DNumFaces`, `ST_3DCentroid`, `ST_3DDistance`, `ST_3DValidationReport(solid) → STRUCT(is_valid BOOLEAN, is_closed BOOLEAN, is_manifold BOOLEAN, is_oriented BOOLEAN, solid_count BIGINT, shell_count BIGINT, face_count BIGINT, open_edge_count BIGINT, non_manifold_edge_count BIGINT, degenerate_face_count BIGINT, code VARCHAR, message VARCHAR)`.
- **`ST_3DVolume` raises on an unclosed solid and one such row fails the whole statement.** Everything else (`ST_3DSurfaceArea`, `ST_3DFootprintArea`, `ST_3DZMin/ZMax`, `ST_3DIsClosed/Manifold/Oriented`, `ST_3DBounds`, `ST_3DNumShells/Faces`) returns a value on an invalid solid. Verified on `fixtures/two-buildings.city.json`: `NL.IMBAG.Pand.0001` is an INVALID Solid (not closed, 2 open edges, 1 non-manifold edge, orientation inconsistent; envelope 388, footprint 80, zmin 0, zmax 8.4); `NL.IMBAG.Pand.0002` is VALID (volume 2178, envelope 1013.4, footprint 180, zmin 0, zmax 12.1).
- `NL.IMBAG.Pand.0001-part1` is a MultiSurface (WKB "MultiPolygon Z"): `ST_3DTryFromWKB` → NULL. Every `three_d` function returns NULL on a NULL solid, and **`ST_3DValidationReport(NULL)` is NULL**, so `r.is_valid` is NULL rather than false — the "not a solid" row is told apart from the "invalid" row by `s IS NULL`, never by the report. `ST_3DTryFromWKB` on garbage bytes → NULL; on NULL → NULL.
- The one-statement shape that works, verified verbatim (and `read_cityjsonseq(..., lod => '2.2')` behaves identically):

  ```sql
  SELECT id, COALESCE(feature_id, id) AS f, cityjson_wkb_geometry_type(geometry_lod2_2) AS wkb_type, s IS NOT NULL AS parsed,
         r.is_valid, r.is_closed, r.is_manifold, r.is_oriented, r.open_edge_count, r.non_manifold_edge_count, r.degenerate_face_count,
         CASE WHEN r.is_valid THEN ST_3DVolume(s) END AS volume, ST_3DSurfaceArea(s) AS envelope, ST_3DFootprintArea(s) AS footprint,
         ST_3DZMin(s) AS zmin, ST_3DZMax(s) AS zmax
  FROM (SELECT id, feature_id, geometry_lod2_2, ST_3DTryFromWKB(geometry_lod2_2) AS s, ST_3DValidationReport(ST_3DTryFromWKB(geometry_lod2_2)) AS r
        FROM read_cityjson('two.city.json', lod => '2.2') WHERE id IN ('NL.IMBAG.Pand.0001', …))
  ```

- `read_cityjson(name, lod => 'X')` REQUIRES the file's OWN LoD label (`'2.2'`; `'2'` fails with "LOD '2.0' not found in file. Available LODs: 2.2") and names the column `geometry_lod2_2` (label with `.` → `_`), plus `geometry_properties_lod2_2 STRUCT(type VARCHAR, surfaces VARCHAR, face_semantics INTEGER[], shells INTEGER[][])` whose `type` is the CityJSON geometry type ("Solid", "MultiSurface").
- The `cityjson` extension has two cheap WKB helpers that need no `three_d`: `cityjson_wkb_geometry_type(blob) → VARCHAR` ("PolyhedralSurface Z" for a Solid, "MultiPolygon Z" for a MultiSurface) and `cityjson_wkb_extent(blob) → STRUCT(xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax)`.
- **Not yet probed, and Task 1 answers it:** `ST_3DTryFromWKB` on a **CompositeSolid** — no fixture in the repo carried one, so Decisions recorded item 4 settled that Task 1 ADDS `fixtures/composite-solid.city.json` (two unit cubes sharing a face, members' volumes summing to 2) and asserts the parse, the validity report and the summed volume on it. No case skips for want of a fixture.

### What real DuckDB 1.5.5 does with `spatial`

- `ST_GeomFromWKB` parses the reader's **MultiPolygon Z** (LoD 0) WKB, keeping Z; `ST_Area` is the 2D area; `ST_Intersects` / `ST_Within` / `ST_Distance` / `ST_Intersection` / `ST_Centroid` / `ST_Union_Agg` / `ST_Force2D` all accept Z geometries. It **RAISES "Unsupported geometry type in WKB" on a PolyhedralSurface Z**.
- `ST_MakeEnvelope(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)` and `ST_Point(x, y)` build the extent-rectangle and extent-centre proxies from the table's `bbox` struct (which every layer kind has — `layerTables.ts:642-653` forces the STRUCT type on the flat path too).
- **`ST_GeomFromGeoJSON` on a Polygon with `[]` coordinates returns an EMPTY geometry, not NULL and not an error.** Preflight must test `ST_IsEmpty(geom)` as well as `geom IS NULL`. `ST_GeomFromGeoJSON(NULL)` → NULL. `ST_GeomFromText(wkt)` works.
- A GeoJSON FeatureCollection registered as a buffer reads with `read_json('gj.json', columns={type:'VARCHAR', features:'STRUCT(type VARCHAR, properties JSON, geometry JSON)[]'})` + `unnest(features)`; properties read back with `props->>'name'` (VARCHAR) and `(props->>'n')::DOUBLE`; `json_keys(props)` lists them. `LEFT JOIN … ON ST_Intersects(b.g, s.geom)`, `ST_Area(ST_Intersection(…))` for largest overlap, and `MIN(ST_Distance(…))` + `arg_min(s.idx, ST_Distance(…))` over a CROSS JOIN for nearest all work.
- `ST_Transform` exists; the design does not use it (Global Constraints).
- The M2 DECIMAL trap stands: **CAST to DOUBLE before a `median()`**.

### The run queue, the executor contract and the tool definition

- `src/features/processing/types.ts:18-80` — `ToolDefinition` is `{ id, name, group, description, longDescription, extension, needsReader, target: "city" | "vector", needsVectorSource, needsLod, defaultPrefix, outputColumns?, validateParams?, normaliseParams?, implemented }`. **`outputColumns` returns `string[]`** (`types.ts:53-56`), with no type information.
- `src/ui/processing/ToolView.tsx:81-93` — `submitRun({ …, columns: f.columns.map((name) => ({ name, type: "DOUBLE" as const })) })`. **The UI hard-codes `DOUBLE` for every column.** M2's plan said "do not refactor it in M2"; M3 retires that note in Task 4, because Validate solids writes BOOLEAN and Join writes VARCHAR/BOOLEAN/DOUBLE by inference.
- `src/insights/computedColumns.ts:30-34` — `ColumnType = "DOUBLE" | "BOOLEAN" | "VARCHAR"`; `OutputColumn = { name, type }`. The write path already honours the type: `buildAddColumnSql` (`:40-42`) interpolates `col.type`.
- `runQueue.ts:75-83` — `RunRequest = { toolId, targetLayerId, scope, lod, params, prefix, columns: ReadonlyArray<OutputColumn> }`. **There is no source-layer field**: `queueRun` hard-codes `sourceLayerId: null, sourceName: null` (`runQueue.ts:367-368`) even though `RunRecord` carries both (`types.ts:130-131`).
- `runQueue.ts:97-122` — `ToolContext = { table: LayerTable; layer: Layer; featureIds: ReadonlyArray<string> | null; signal: AbortSignal; query(label, sql): Promise<QueryOutcome>; phase(p: RunPhase): void; warn(text: string): void; throwIfCancelled(): void }`. `featureIds` are **ROW ids** already expanded to whole features by `resolveScope` (`scope.ts:126-138`, `sql.ts:488-496`), or `null` for "every row".
- `runQueue.ts:124-131` — `ToolResult = { columns: ReadonlyArray<OutputColumn>; rows: ReadonlyMap<string, Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>; measured: number; skipped: ReadonlyArray<SkipCount> }`. `runQueue.ts:133-136` — `ToolExecutor = (run: RunRecord, ctx: ToolContext) => Promise<ToolResult>`.
- `types.ts:84` — `RunPhase = "extension" | "source" | "compute" | "write"`. **`"source"` is never entered today**: the only `ctx.phase` calls are `heightFromExtent.ts:163` and `roofMetrics.ts:234`, both `"compute"`. Its label already exists: `runFormat.ts:13` → `{ key: "source", label: "Reading source" }`.
- Phase transitions in `execute`: `runQueue.ts:504` the one `startedAt`; `:583` `"extension"` (only when `tool.extension !== null && !isExtensionLoaded(...)`, `:582`); `:637-642` `"compute"` with `featureIds`/`scopeCount`; `:703` `"write"`. Pre-flight refusals before any phase: layer gone `"Layer removed"` (`:509-516`), no table (`:517-525`), table renamed `"Layer changed while running; run again"` (`:529-536`), a column that now belongs to the source data (`:552-560`), no executor `"Not available yet"` (`:561-569`).
- `runQueue.ts:675-680` — the record is re-read immediately before `executor(record, ctx)` and the result goes through `canonicalise(result, table.columns)` (`:256-283`), so **the table's spelling of a column wins**.
- The write (`runQueue.ts:703-739` → `computedColumns.ts:144-214`) is ONE transaction: `BEGIN` → optional `CREATE TABLE "__undo_<runId>" AS SELECT "id", <replaced…>` → `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` per column → `UPDATE … FROM read_json_auto('__vals_<runId>.json') AS v WHERE t."id" = v."id"` → the ONE cancel check (`computedColumns.ts:199-202`) → `COMMIT`, with `dropBuffer(valuesFile)` in a `finally` (`:209-213`).
- Publication after the commit (`runQueue.ts:741-857`): `mergeAttributes(layer.id, merge)`, per-column `setProvenance`, Undo stolen from any earlier run sharing a column (`:783-800`), `undoState.set` (`:802-813`), `raced(refreshLayerTableColumns(layer.id), null)` (`:823`), then the terminal `patch`.
- `undoRun` (`runQueue.ts:932-1006`) runs on `runOnTableQueue` (`:936`), re-validates at the head (`:942-943`), races `undoComputedColumns` (`:951`) and `refreshLayerTableColumns` (`:972`) against death — and **on an `EngineDeadError` from the post-COMMIT refresh it still falls through to publish the restored model, the provenance rollback and the "Undone" card** (`:971-1005`). This is the M2 parked residual, carried here (§Task list, engine-death hardening).
- `installEngineWatcher` (`runQueue.ts:1094-1143`) keys on the `ready → failed` transition; `installStaleWatcher` (`:1153-1176`) fires on a table-name change or `building → ready` and marks done runs of that layer `stale`.
- `scope.ts:52-62` — `ScopeResolution` carries `featureIds` (ROW ids, `null` = every row), `count` (FEATURES in scope) and `total` (FEATURES on the layer). `resolveScope` refuses before querying: "No filter applied", "Nothing selected on this layer", "Nothing to run on (0 buildings)" (`:97-132`).
- `eligibility.ts:40-85` — `toolEligibility(tool, ctx)` in order: `!implemented` → engine failed → target kind (`target === "city"` wants `targetKind` `"city"`/`"streaming"`; otherwise `targetKind !== "vector"` → `"Needs a vector layer"`) → `needsReader && !hasReader` → `needsReader && !sourceAvailable` → `needsVectorSource && !hasVectorLayer` → extension failed → table failed. `EligibilityContext` (`:10-29`) already carries `targetKind`, `hasReader`, `sourceAvailable`, `hasVectorLayer` and `extensionState`.
- `toolRegistry.ts:5-119` — all seven tools exist. `measure-solids` (`:28-42`) and `validate-solids` (`:43-57`) already declare `extension: "three_d"`, `needsReader: true`, `needsLod: true`, `defaultPrefix: "solid_"`. `join-by-location` (`:74-88`) and `distance-to-nearest` (`:104-118`) declare `extension: "spatial"`, `needsVectorSource: true`, `defaultPrefix: ""`. `aggregate-per-area` (`:89-103`) declares `target: "vector"`, `defaultPrefix: "bld_"`, `needsVectorSource: false`. All five are `implemented: false` and none has `outputColumns`.
- `src/ui/processing/useLodOptions.ts:47-55` — `if (tool.id !== "roof-metrics") return NO_LOD;`. `LodChoices = { options: ReadonlyArray<LodOption>; noun: string; emptyReason: string | null }` (`:26-32`). `roofLodOptions(layer)` (`roofGeometrySource.ts:193-230`) is tags-only, applies the contributor rule, counts FEATURES and sorts by `parseFloat` descending. `LodOption = { lod: string; features: number }` (`roofGeometrySource.ts:132-136`).
- `src/features/processing/roofGeometrySource.ts:52-62` — `RoofGeometrySource` is `{ has(objectId); hasGeometryAt(objectId, lod); roofSurfacesAt(objectId, lod) }`, memoised per `` `${id} ${lod}` ``, static branch at `:94-118` and streaming branch at `:67-92`. `lodTagsByObject(layer)` (`:145-170`) is the tags-only walk.
- `src/ui/processing/RunFooter.tsx:241` — `const styleColumn = run.columns[0]`; `:46-53` `readMedian`; `:127-142` the draft: `setDraft(layerId, { editingId: null, open: true, form: { name: column, color: NEW_RULE_COLOR_HEX, logic: "AND", conditions: [{ field: column, operator: ">", value }] } })`, then **`updateLayer(layerId, { colorBy: "rules" })` eagerly at `:141`**, then `requestSection(layerId, "style")`. `:256-258` — disabled with `"stale: layer reloaded"` (outranks) or `"All values are empty"` on `summary.firstColumnNonNull === 0`.
- The rule schema already expresses everything M3 needs: `ConditionOperator = ">" | "<" | "=" | ">=" | "<="` and `Condition.value: number | string | boolean` (`packages/cityjson-navara-plugins/packages/navara-core/src/rules/types.ts:10-15`). A BOOLEAN `=` rule and a text `=` rule are schema-legal; what Task 9 must check in the browser is the EDITOR's value input for a boolean field.
- `src/scene/cityColors.ts:81` — `NEW_RULE_COLOR_HEX = "#7cb518"`, the one colour every draft takes today. `:117-126` — `CATEGORY_PALETTE_HEX`, eight categorical colours used by "Color by attribute". `cityColors.ts`'s collision rule (pinned by `tests/unit/scene/cityColors.test.ts`) is the constraint any new rule palette must satisfy.

### The engine seam, the FIFO, and what a "Reading source" phase can reach

- `duckdb.ts:681-693` — **`runQuery` returns `{ ok: false, message }`, it never throws**, and `ddl` (`:695-697`) IS `runQuery`. There is no DDL/DML distinction at the seam.
- `duckdb.ts:150-187` — `markEngineDead` bumps `generation` first (`:154`), clears `extensionPromises` (`:158`), fires and DROPS each `onEngineDeath` listener (`:163-170`, one-shot per engine), nulls `db`/`conn` (`:174-175`), clears `initPromise` (`:178`) and publishes `failed` LAST (`:185`). `getEngineGeneration()` at `:232`.
- `engineAwait.ts:70-100` — `raced(promise, signal | null)`; `:104-106` `racedWithDeath(promise)`. Documented limit: `onEngineDeath` fires once per engine and drops its waiters as it fires, so a `raced` STARTED after the death hears nothing — every `duckdb.ts` primitive answers immediately once the engine is gone, so the hazard is only the await already in flight.
- **The racing asymmetry, and the whole of group D:** `layerTables.ts:80-98` shadows `runQuery`, `ddl`, `registerBuffer`, `dropBuffer` and `initDuckDB` with `racedWithDeath` wrappers so a call site cannot reach the unraced primitive by accident. **`computedColumns.ts:20-27` and `export.ts:20` import the UNRACED primitives**, and so does every off-queue caller (the export dialog and writer, `useLayerCounts`, the grid query, the map-filter sync, the Stats tab, `RunFooter`'s median).
- `layerTables.ts:420-436` — `enqueue` is `chain.then(task, task)` (reject-tolerant), and **`runOnTableQueue` IS `enqueue`**. `enqueueLayerTable` also goes through `enqueue` (`:1200`), so **a run already inside its FIFO slot must never call `enqueueLayerTable` — that is a deadlock**, which is why a derived layer's table is built by the run itself (Design decision (f)).
- `layerTables.ts:1089` — the table name is `` `layer_${++counter}` ``, minted INSIDE the queued task; `counter` is module-private (`:306`).
- `layerTables.ts:166-182` — `LayerTable = { table, sourceName, source: SourceProvider | null, reader: "read_cityjson" | "read_cityjsonseq" | null, columns, lods, rowCount }`. **There is no `extension` field and no byte count.** The reader's VFS name is `` `${table}.${source.extension}` `` (`:596`), and `LayerTableSource` kind `"bytes"` carries `extension: ReaderExtension` (`"city.json" | "city.jsonl"`, `:131`, `:151`) and `provider: SourceProvider | null` (`:156`).
- `layerTables.ts:119` — `SourceProvider = () => Promise<Uint8Array>`, returning a FRESH array per call because `registerBuffer` DETACHES what it is given (`duckdb.ts:701-711`, `:724-738`). A name read after `dropBuffer` still RESOLVES, to garbage (`duckdb.ts:717-722`), so callers mint a fresh VFS name per load and never read one they dropped.
- `columnKind.ts:90-95` — `LodColumn = { label, suffix }`; `label` is `"2.2"` and `suffix` is the reader's own spelling `"2_2"`. `lodsFromColumnNames` (`:104-120`) builds them from the described `geometry_lod*` names. **Never re-spell a suffix** — `"0.0"` and `"0"` are different columns and only the file knows which it has.
- `export.ts:558-578` is the working model for a "Reading source" phase: `const bytes = await request.source();` → `registerBuffer(sourceName, bytes)` → ONE `CREATE TABLE <scratch>.src AS SELECT … FROM <reader>(<sourceName>)` → `await dropBuffer(sourceName)` the moment the parse is done, with a second `dropBuffer` in the `finally` (`:658`). `CityParquetExportRequest` (`:386-403`) carries `sourceExtension: string` because `LayerTable` does not.
- `export.ts:76-96` — `validateExportBytes` exists because a VFS name that was never created reads back as ONE GARBAGE BYTE with no error.
- `sql.ts:28-30` `quoteIdent`, `:39-48` `quoteLiteral` (**throws on a non-finite number**), `:438-439` `buildMedianSql` (root rows only), `:451-458` `buildFeatureScopeWhere`, `:488-496` `buildFeatureRowsSql`.

### The city model, the parser and the resident record

- `packages/cityjson-navara-plugins/packages/navara-core/src/citymodel/types.ts:105-118` — `Surface` is `{ type: BuildingSurfaceType; rings; attributes; lod: string | null; material?; texture? }`. **There is NO geometry-type tag**, so the spec's "every surface is tagged with its LoD and its geometry type" (§6) is not yet true.
- `.../citymodel/cityjson/parseHelpers.ts:230-284` — `extractSurfaces(geom, realVertices, objectBBox, lod, ctx)` switches on `geom.type` with cases `"MultiSurface"` / `"CompositeSurface"` (`:255-259`), `"Solid"` (`:260-267`), `"MultiSolid"` / `"CompositeSolid"` (`:268-280`) and a `default: break` (`:281`). `lod` is already threaded through to `buildSurface`; the geometry type is the one fact `visit` does not carry.
- `.../navara-flatcitybuf/src/workerProtocol.ts:39-51` — `ResidentObjectRecord` carries `geometryLods` (M2) but nothing solid-specific, and **no boundaries at all**. Irrelevant for the solids tools (they need a reader, which a streaming layer never has); decisive for a derived layer of a streaming parent (Design decision (f); the owner accepted the deviation — Decisions recorded item 1).
- `src/features/streaming/openStreamingLayer.ts:109-115` — a streaming layer's `model.objects` is `{}`.

### The UI, the layer stores and the vector path

- **There is no `CityLayer` type**; it is `Layer` (`layerStore.ts:28-132`). The store holds an ARRAY only (`:134-136`) — no active id, no z-order. `addLayer` (`:139-187`, impl `:326-379`) **appends** (`:347-349`); there is **no layer reorder, no rename action** (rename is `updateLayer(id, { name })`, `:189-197`) and **no palette action**. Ids: `input.id ?? crypto.randomUUID()` (`:327`) — `id` is ALREADY an optional field of `addLayer`'s input (`:158-161`, added for `openStreamingLayer`), which is what lets Task 21's `publish()` mint the id first and adopt the table before the row exists.
- The active layer lives in `useWorkspaceStore.activeLayerId` (`workspaceStore.ts:19`, setter `:67-71`, which clears a selection belonging to another layer). The public door is `activateLayer(id)` (`features/workspace/layerCoordination.ts:34`); `unifiedLayerOrder` puts every city layer before every geo layer (`activeLayer.ts:30-35`).
- `addCityLayer.ts:139-165` — `addCityLayer(input)` adds the row, then **fire-and-forget** `void enqueueLayerTable(layerId, input.duckdb).catch(warn)` (`:154-164`). **It does not activate the layer.** `modelTableSource` (`:96-120`) chooses `{kind:"model"}` for CityGML or byte-less input, else `{kind:"bytes", reader, extension, provider}`.
- `layerTableLifecycle.ts` — `rebuildWanted(layerId)` is `tablePanelOpen || processing.open || runInFlightFor(layerId)` (`:113-116`); `sweepStreamingLayers()` (`:202-214`) runs on the table-panel and processing subscriptions (`:216-234`) and is **unconditional**, which is the M2 residual that retires a finished card as stale. `knownVersions` is the map to compare against.
- **proj4 is called in exactly ONE place**: `src/scene/cursorCrsReadout.ts:68`. The reusable door is `crsFromGeodetic(lngDeg, latDeg, height, epsg): readonly [number, number, number] | null` (`:53-79`) — 2-D only (height passes through), guarded by the SYNCHRONOUS `ensureProjDef(epsg)` (`:59`), and returning `null` (never NaN) on a non-finite input or a proj4 throw. Its companion is `epsgForLayer(referenceSystem): number | null` (`:35-41`). The ASYNC warm-up for a code proj4 does not yet know is `ensureModelCrsLoadable(model)` (`ensureCrs.ts:32-48`); until something awaits it, `crsFromGeodetic` returns `null` for that code. `features/` may import from `scene/` (`geoLayers/categorize.ts:26-29` already does).
- `geoLayerStore.ts:89-101` — `GeoLayer` is a discriminated union on `kind`; the geojson config is `{ data?, url?, preparedData?, preparation?, preparationError?, preparationEpoch? }` (`:36-47`). **`GeoLayerPatch` (`:120-130`) deliberately excludes `config`**; the only config writers are `relinkGeoJsonLayer` (`:278-292`, which DROPS `url` and `preparationEpoch`) and `setPreparedGeoJson` (`:294-309`, which spreads into a NEW config object). **There is no geo analogue of `mergeAttributes`.**
- `config.preparedData` is documented "Engine-only normalized clone; **never persisted**" (`geoLayerStore.ts:42-43`) and is what the engine (`geoLayerDescriptions.ts:55-57`, `geoSourceDescription`), the records panel (`GeoRecordsPanel.tsx:25`) and the GeoJSON export (`GeoLayerExport.tsx:24`) all read. **"Color by attribute" is the exception**: it reads the RAW document (`GeoStyleControls.tsx:190-193, 198-217`), so a property written only into `preparedData` would paint and tabulate but not appear in its select.
- `geoJsonRecords.ts:2` — `GEO_STABLE_FEATURE_KEY = "__roofy_stable_feature_id"`, stamped as a `StableFeatureEnvelope` (`:4-8`, `:66-84`); `readGeoStableFeatureId(properties)` (`:11-21`), `normalizeGeoJsonDocument(document)` (`:33-95`), `publicGeoProperties(properties)` (`:98-114`). `geoRecords.ts:5-53` — `GEO_RECORD_ID` symbol, `geoRecords(document)`, `geoRecordColumns(records)` (types `DOUBLE` if any row's value is a number, else `VARCHAR`).
- `geoLayerSync.ts:524` — the engine pair is torn down and rebuilt when `entry.config !== layer.config || entry.kind !== layer.kind`; visibility/opacity/style alone take the cheap `Layer.update()` path (`:539-557`). So ONE config replacement per run is ONE rebuild.
- **No computed badge on geo rows today**: `GeoRecordsPanel.tsx:118-144` passes neither `layerId` nor `derivedColumnNames` to `DataGrid` (whose gates are `DataGrid.tsx:54-58, 83-89, 140-146`). `GeoFeatureDetails.tsx:20-28` renders a bare `AttrRow` list with **no COMPUTED group, no badge, no provenance** — unlike `LayerAttributesSection.tsx:42-82`, which has all three for city layers.
- `useComputedColumnStore.byLayer` is `Record<layerId, Record<column, Provenance>>` (`computedColumns.ts:265-274`) with nothing city-specific: **a geo layer id works as a key unchanged.**
- Rules: `evaluateCondition` (`@cityjson/navara-core` `dist/index.js:1191-1199`) makes `"="` a **strict `===`** and every ordering operator `false` unless both sides are numbers. `RulesEditor.tsx:755-774` coerces the typed literals `true`/`false` to booleans. **A BOOLEAN `=` rule works end to end today**; Validate solids needs no editor change.
- `RulesEditor.tsx:809-816` — `defaultRuleFormValues()` hard-codes `NEW_RULE_COLOR_HEX`; nothing rotates. `ensureRulesMode()` (`:158-165`) flips `colorBy` to `"rules"` only **from `"surface"`**, never from `"single"` — which is the shape Task 26 copies for Style by result's Save.
- `layerPresentation.ts:105-136` — `layerStateLine(input)` is the ONE place a layer's state sentence is worded; `cityStateLine` (`:128-136`) produces `"312 buildings · LoD 2.2"`. `LayerRowMenu.tsx:158-205` renders exactly four items: Zoom to layer, Open table, Rename, Remove.
- `ExportDialog.tsx:67-81, 172-179` — city formats are `cityparquet | parquet | csv | json`, with CityParquet offered only when `table.reader !== null && table.source !== null && table.lods.length > 0 && epsg !== null`. **A derived reader-backed layer therefore gets CityParquet for free if it carries a reader, a provider and lods.** `GeoLayerExport.tsx:54-93` already offers GeoJSON + CSV for a geojson layer, reading `preparedData`.
- `App.tsx:1061-1078` is the ONLY place a city layer is serialised (an explicit field list — a new `Layer` field is not persisted unless it is added there); `:1045-1056` computes `activeLayer` as an INDEX into `allLayers`/`allGeoLayers`; `:1103-1108` is the Save toast. `captureSnapshot.ts:112-127` just passes them through. `SNAPSHOT_VERSION = "4"` (`persistence/types.ts:465`).
- `ToolView.tsx:236-255` already renders the **Write to** field as a single checked, disabled radio with no Name input; `:220-233` dispatches PARAMETERS by a literal `toolId === "roof-metrics"` equality test. `useToolForm.ts:183-185` — `runReason = !eligibility.ok ? eligibility.reason : (lods.emptyReason ?? prefixError ?? paramsError ?? scopeReason)`.
- `LogView.tsx:42-62` — the run header rows; **`["Building geometry", "—"]` at `:51` is a hard-coded placeholder** (same in `runFormat.ts:89`) waiting for the cross-layer proxy. `:95-104` renders each `LogEntry.sql` in a `<pre>`; the write step logs `sql: null` (`runQueue.ts:726-731`), which is the M1 leftover.
- `RecentRuns.tsx:50-53` already composes `` `${run.targetName} ← ${run.sourceName}` `` when `sourceName` is set — the field that `queueRun` hard-codes to `null`.
- `RoofMetricsParams.tsx:22-28` is the params-section template: an inline props type `{ params: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; onChange: (next: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>) => void }`, no store access, normalise-in and write-back-whole.

## New exported names — the contract every task codes against

Three expansion planners write task bodies in parallel from the index below. **These are the names and types; a task's Interfaces block repeats this text verbatim and never paraphrases it.**

```ts
// packages/…/navara-core/src/citymodel/types.ts  (Task 2 — plugin submodule)
// Surface gains:
//   geometryType?: CityJSONGeometryType | null
//       The CityJSON geometry TYPE the surface was extracted from ("Solid",
//       "MultiSurface", …). OPTIONAL as well as nullable (Decisions item 6
//       (vi)): absent and null both read "unknown", so the 21 files of
//       hand-built `Surface` literals stay untouched. `buildSurface` writes
//       `geometryType: geom.type`; `navara-cityparquet`'s `decodeTable.ts`
//       writes `geometryType: null` explicitly. Task 3 is the one consumer.

// src/features/processing/types.ts  (Task 4, Task 9, Task 11, Task 20)
export type ToolDestination = "layer" | "new";
export type StyleValueSource =
  | { readonly kind: "median" }
  | { readonly kind: "mostFrequent" }
  | { readonly kind: "literal"; readonly value: number | string | boolean };
export interface StyleByResult {
  /** "rule" opens the rule editor on a draft; "attribute" opens a vector
   *  layer's Color by attribute on the picked column (spec §7.6). */
  readonly kind: "rule" | "attribute";
  /**
   * The rule's operator. A FUNCTION of the picked column for §7.5, whose rule
   * is `=` on a copied TEXT field but `>` on `<prefix>matches_n` when no text
   * field was copied — two operators chosen by which column `pick` returned.
   * The five descriptors that need only one operator pass it plainly.
   */
  readonly operator:
    | ConditionOperator
    | ((picked: OutputColumn) => ConditionOperator);
  /** The same union, for the same §7.5 reason: `mostFrequent` on a text field,
   *  a `0` literal on `<prefix>matches_n`. Unused for `kind: "attribute"`. */
  readonly value:
    | StyleValueSource
    | ((picked: OutputColumn) => StyleValueSource);
  /** The column to style by, from the ones the run ACTUALLY wrote, in the
   *  tool's own §7 order. Null when the run wrote nothing styleable. */
  readonly pick: (written: ReadonlyArray<OutputColumn>) => OutputColumn | null;
}

/** The ONE place either field is read, so `RunFooter` has no branch and a
 *  plain (non-function) descriptor is returned as it is. */
export function resolveStyleOperator(
  descriptor: StyleByResult,
  picked: OutputColumn,
): ConditionOperator {
  return typeof descriptor.operator === "function"
    ? descriptor.operator(picked)
    : descriptor.operator;
}

export function resolveStyleValueSource(
  descriptor: StyleByResult,
  picked: OutputColumn,
): StyleValueSource {
  return typeof descriptor.value === "function"
    ? descriptor.value(picked)
    : descriptor.value;
}

// FrozenRequest gains (module-private, computed ONCE in submitRun):

//       layer whose TABLE the run reads and whose FIFO slot it holds, so EVERY
//       existing read of `targetLayerId` inside the queue moves to it: the scope

// src/features/geoLayers/geoLayerStore.ts  (Task 11)
/** The union's GeoJSON arm. Every reader of a vector layer's CONTENT reads
 *  `config.preparedData`, which only this arm has. */
export type GeoJsonLayer = Extract<GeoLayer, { kind: "geojson" }>;

export type ToolTarget =
  | { readonly kind: "city"; readonly layer: Layer; readonly table: LayerTable }
  | {
      readonly kind: "vector";
      readonly layer: GeoJsonLayer;
      readonly records: ReadonlyArray<GeoRecord>;
    };
export type ToolSource =
  | { readonly kind: "city"; readonly layer: Layer; readonly table: LayerTable }
  | {
      readonly kind: "vector";
      readonly layer: GeoJsonLayer;
      readonly table: string;
      readonly propertyKeys: ReadonlyArray<string>;
      readonly skipped: number;
    };
export interface ToolContext {
  /** The layer whose TABLE the compute reads. For a vector-TARGET tool this is
   *  the SOURCE city layer; for every other tool it is `target.layer`. The two
   *  M2 executors read only these and are unaffected. */
  readonly layer: Layer;
  readonly table: LayerTable;
  readonly target: ToolTarget; // where the run WRITES
  readonly source: ToolSource | null;
  readonly featureIds: ReadonlyArray<string> | null; // ROW ids of `table`, or null
  readonly signal: AbortSignal;
  query(label: string, sql: string): Promise<QueryOutcome>;
  phase(p: RunPhase): void;
  warn(text: string): void;
  throwIfCancelled(): void;
}
// ToolResult (Task 7 — the ONE caveat channel, Decisions item 6 (i)) gains two
// optional fields and nothing else. `rows` is keyed by object id for a city
// target and by the GeoJSON stable feature id
// (geoJsonRecords.GEO_STABLE_FEATURE_KEY) for a vector target.
//   line?: string
//       The card's OWN first phrase when "N buildings measured" is wrong for
//       this tool ("1,143 buildings joined", "1,079 valid"). Task 7 declares;
//       Tasks 10, 16 and 19 set it.
//   caveats?: ReadonlyArray<SkipCount>
//       §6.2's "evaluated WITH A CAVEAT" — values were written, so these are
//       not skips. `summarise` renders each as "<count> <cause>" BETWEEN the
//       measured count and the skipped count, so a cause carries no number of
//       its own. Task 7 declares and makes the one `summarise` edit; Tasks 10,
//       16, 17 and 19 set it. No other task re-declares either field.

## Design decisions

### (a) Solid geometry is a surface TAG, and the LoD select reads tags only

**Decision: `Surface` gains `geometryType?: CityJSONGeometryType | null` — OPTIONAL as well as nullable — in the plugin submodule, set once in `buildSurface` from the geometry it is being built from; `solidLodOptions` then answers "has a SOLID at LoD X" the same tags-only way `roofLodOptions` answers its question. CityParquet's independently built surfaces carry `null`.**

The spec assumes this already ("every surface is tagged with its LoD and its geometry type", §6) and it is not true: `Surface` (`navara-core/src/citymodel/types.ts:105-118`) has `type` (semantic) and `lod`, and nothing about the geometry it came from. M2's constraint — nothing walks a whole layer's geometry synchronously — forbids the obvious alternative of asking the reader, because the LoD select is drawn before any source is re-read and on every layer kind.

**The change is one line in one function.** `extractSurfaces` (`parseHelpers.ts:231-287`) has five surface-producing cases and they all funnel through `buildSurface`, which already receives `geom` as its first parameter; the object literal at `:184-189` gains `geometryType: geom.type` and the inline annotation at `:177-183` gains the field. No case is touched. `parseCityObject` is the funnel for CityJSON, CityJSONSeq **and** FlatCityBuf (`fcb.worker.ts:305`), so three formats get the tag for free.

**Why `| null` and not required.** `navara-cityparquet/src/decodeTable.ts:725-733` builds `Surface` objects itself, from a flat face list whose `GeometryColumnRef` carries only `{ name, lod }` — CityParquet genuinely has no geometry-type information at that point. A required non-null field would make that file lie; `null` makes it say "unknown", which is the honest answer and which `solidLodOptions` reads as "not a solid" — matching the eligibility reason a CityParquet layer already gets for the solids tools ("Needs a CityJSON or CityJSONSeq source…", `eligibility.ts:55-63`), so no user-visible verdict changes.

**Why OPTIONAL and not just nullable** (commander's ruling, Decisions item 6 (vi)). `grep -rln 'type: "RoofSurface"\|type: "WallSurface"\|type: "GroundSurface"' src tests packages/*/packages/*/{src,tests}` finds **21 files** of hand-built `Surface` literals (10 app test files, 11 submodule test files). A required `| null` field stops every one of them compiling, for a distinction that buys nothing: the ONE consumer is Task 3's `hasSolidAt`, which asks `geometryType === "Solid" | "CompositeSolid" | "MultiSolid"`, and absent and `null` answer it identically. `decodeTable.ts` still writes `geometryType: null` EXPLICITLY, because CityParquet has genuinely LOST the information and writing that down is what stops a later reader assuming the omission was an oversight.

**Alternatives rejected.** (i) A per-object `solidLods: string[]` roll-up on `CityObject`, mirroring `ResidentObjectRecord.geometryLods`: cheaper to read, but it answers exactly one question and the next tool would want another roll-up; the surface tag answers every "geometry of kind K at LoD L" question the toolbox will ever ask, at the same cost. (ii) Reading `geometry_properties_lod<X>.type` from the reader: correct, and it is what the RUN uses to tell "not a solid" from "invalid" — but it needs the source re-read, which is the one thing the LoD select may not do. (iii) Inferring from the semantic mix (a Solid has a GroundSurface): a guess, and 3D BAG's LoD 1.2 MultiSurfaces have ground surfaces too.

**Streaming layers need nothing.** The solids tools declare `needsReader: true` and a streaming layer never has a reader (`eligibility.ts:55-63` refuses it first), so `ResidentObjectRecord` gains no field.

**Cost if wrong:** one optional field on a submodule interface and one wrapper function to revert.

### (b) The "Reading source" phase re-registers the parent's bytes, once per run, and drops them the moment the parse is done

**Decision: `readSource({ runId, table, lod, signal })` mints the VFS name `` `${table.table}_${runId}.${table.extension}` ``, calls `table.source!()` for a FRESH array, `registerBuffer`s it, and returns a `ReadSourceHandle` whose `from` is `` `${table.reader}(${quoteLiteral(name)}, lod => ${quoteLiteral(lodLabel)})` `` and whose `geometryColumn` is `` `geometry_lod${lodColumn.suffix}` ``. The run calls `handle.release()` in a `finally`. `LayerTable` gains `extension: ReaderExtension | null` and `sourceBytes: number | null`, both captured at build.**

`export.ts:558-578` is the working precedent and the shape is copied from it, including the `dropBuffer` the moment the one `CREATE`/`SELECT` has parsed — a 300 MB CityJSON must not sit in the wasm heap for the length of a compute.

**The LoD label → column mapping must come from `LodColumn`, never from string surgery.** `read_cityjson(name, lod => 'X')` requires the file's OWN label, and the column it names is the label with `.` → `_`: `"2.2"` → `geometry_lod2_2`. `LayerTable.lods` already carries `{ label, suffix }` straight from the described names (`columnKind.ts:90-120`), and `"0.0"` and `"0"` are different columns that only the file distinguishes. `readSource` therefore looks the label up in `table.lods` and uses that entry's `suffix`; a label with no entry is an error, not a guess.

**Why `LayerTable` gains two fields.** The extension is reconstructible only by parsing `sourceName` (`` `${table}.${extension}` ``, `layerTables.ts:596`), which is exactly the fragility `export.ts` routed around by making its CALLER pass `sourceExtension: string` — a loose string where a `ReaderExtension` union exists. One field at the build site (`buildFromReader`'s return, `:618-628`) fixes both callers. And §6's workload note ("Re-reads a 180 MB source; this can take a minute and needs memory" above 100 MB) needs a byte count that exists nowhere: `source.bytes.byteLength` read BEFORE `registerBuffer` detaches it (`:597`) is the only honest number, and it is one line. Both are `| null` because the flat-fallback path has neither.

**Alternatives rejected.** (i) Keeping the bytes for the run's duration so a second statement need not re-register: the run issues exactly one statement per tool, and holding the array is the memory hazard §6's note exists to warn about. (ii) Threading the extension through `RunRequest` the way `export.ts` threads it through its request: it pushes a fact about the table into the run's frozen parameters, where a rebuilt table would make it stale. (iii) Re-reading the source into a scratch TABLE first (`export.ts`'s shape): right when several statements read it, wasteful when one does.

**Cost if wrong:** two nullable fields and one module.

### (c) One cross-layer run shape: the city table is the compute ground, the vector layer is a per-run table, and a vector target's results live in its feature properties

**Decision: every cross-layer run occupies the CITY layer's slot on the one table FIFO and computes over the city table (`ctx.table`), whatever the destination. The vector layer becomes `__src_<runId>`, created in the `"source"` phase from an app-built NDJSON of reprojected features and dropped in a `finally`. A vector TARGET's results are merged into `config.preparedData` through one new store action; provenance goes in `useComputedColumnStore` under the geo layer's id; Undo puts the run's OWN columns back into the current document, on the same table FIFO.**

There is ONE queue, not one per layer (`layerTables.ts:417-419`), so "which layer's FIFO" is not a real choice — what matters is that the run holds the queue for its whole life so no rebuild of the city table can move underneath it, which `runOnTableQueue(() => execute(…))` (`runQueue.ts:404-406`) already gives unchanged.

**Why the vector layer is a table at all, given the compute could be done in JS.** The predicates, the largest-overlap area and the nearest-distance search are exactly what `spatial` is for, and §7.5-§7.7's semantics (boundary-inclusive `within`, `ST_Area(ST_Intersection(...))`, `arg_min` over a cross join) are one statement each in SQL and a geometry library in JS. The app carries no such library and §2 chose the extension.

**Why NDJSON + `registerBuffer` + `read_json` with an explicit `columns=` + `ST_GeomFromText`, and not the two alternatives.** The app reprojects app-side anyway (Global Constraints), so whatever DuckDB reads is a document the app has just built; the question is only its shape. A `VALUES` literal needs no VFS name but puts every ring of every feature into one statement string, which is unbounded and lands verbatim in the run's log. `read_json` of a GeoJSON FeatureCollection with `ST_GeomFromGeoJSON` works (probed) but walks into the verified trap that an empty `coordinates` array yields an EMPTY geometry rather than NULL or an error — a trap preflight has already removed app-side, so paying for it in SQL buys nothing. NDJSON of `{idx, props, wkt}` is the shape `computedColumns.ts:152-186` already uses for the write (`__vals_<runId>.json`), it is one `registerBuffer` and one `dropBuffer`, and `props` reads back with `props->>'name'` and `(props->>'n')::DOUBLE` as the probe pinned. **The read is `read_json(file, format = 'newline_delimited', columns = {… props: 'JSON' …})`, never `read_json_auto`**: auto-inference reads the nested `props` object as a STRUCT, which answers none of those accessors, and a heterogeneous source (one feature with a property, another without) is exactly what inference gets wrong. The explicit `columns=` also pins the other column TYPES, so an `idx` that happens to be uniform cannot come back as something else. (The WRITE path keeps `read_json_auto` over its flat `__vals_<runId>.json`, which has no nested object — that statement is unchanged.)

**Where a vector target's results go, and why not `config.data`.** A geo layer has no DuckDB table and no model; what the app holds is the document. `config.preparedData` is what the ENGINE, the records panel and the GeoJSON export all read (`geoLayerDescriptions.ts:55-57`, `GeoRecordsPanel.tsx:25`, `GeoLayerExport.tsx:24`), and it is documented "never persisted" (`geoLayerStore.ts:42-43`) — which is exactly §8's "nothing new is saved". Writing `config.data` instead would materialise a URL-backed layer's whole fetched document into the layer row and thence into the snapshot, persisting results the spec says are session-only. The one leak is that "Color by attribute" reads the RAW document (`GeoStyleControls.tsx:190-193, 198-217`), so §7.6's "Style by result opens Color by attribute set to the first output column" would find nothing; the fix is to read `preparedData` first there, which is strictly more correct anyway (it is the document every other reader uses).

**One config replacement per run.** `geoLayerSync.ts:524` rebuilds the engine pair on `config` identity, so the merge must be ONE `setState` producing one new config — not one per feature.

**Provenance.** `useComputedColumnStore.byLayer` is `Record<layerId, Record<column, Provenance>>` with nothing city-specific (`computedColumns.ts:265-274`); a geo layer id is a string like any other. The badge and tooltip then need only a consumer on the geo side (Task 18), not a second registry.

**Undo.** What is captured before the merge is, per feature, the value each of THIS run's columns held — with an explicit ABSENT marker for a property that was not there — and the Undo merges those back into whatever the document is by then, through `replaceGeoPreparedData`. That is `UndoState.previousModelValues`' exact analogue, and it is not a document snapshot for a reason: §6.2 steals a run's Undo only where two runs share a COLUMN, so a count run and a sum run on one layer are both undoable at once, and restoring a snapshot taken before the first would erase the second's results while its own card still offered Undo. The Undo runs INSIDE `runOnTableQueue` and re-reads the layer at the head, although it writes no table: a cross-layer run holds that queue for its whole life and has captured this layer's records, so replacing the document underneath it would leave it computing against something nothing on screen shows.

**Cost if wrong:** one store action and one `GeoStyleControls` read to revert.

### (d) Reprojection is app-side, through the app's single proj4 door, and preflight reaches no store and no engine

**Decision: `reprojectGeoLayer(document, epsg, control?)` reaches no store and no engine, walks the document once in BOUNDED BATCHES, and calls `crsFromGeodetic(lng, lat, 0, epsg)` (`src/scene/cursorCrsReadout.ts:53-79`) per coordinate. It yields a macrotask every 500 features and every 20,000 coordinates, calling `control.checkpoint()` (the run's `ctx.throwIfCancelled`) immediately before each yield, so a Cancel lands inside the phase and the frame keeps painting on a 200 MB source. A feature is SKIPPED — and counted — when its geometry is null, has empty coordinates, is unparseable, or when any coordinate fails to project. `ensureModelCrsLoadable(targetModel)` is awaited before the walk, because `crsFromGeodetic`'s guard is synchronous and returns `null` for a definition proj4 has not loaded yet.**

`crsFromGeodetic` is the app's only proj4 call site and already has the three properties preflight needs: it is 2-D (the spec's operations are all 2-D in the target's CRS), it returns `null` rather than NaN on a non-finite input or a proj4 throw, and it is guarded by `ensureProjDef`. Importing it from `features/processing/` is legal and has a precedent (`features/geoLayers/categorize.ts:26-29`).

**The async warm-up is not optional.** A city layer's CRS definition is loaded by `ensureModelCrsLoadable` at layer-add time, but a run must not depend on that having happened for THIS layer in THIS session; awaiting it in the `"source"` phase costs nothing when it is already loaded and is the difference between "4 areas skipped" and "every area skipped" on a cold definition.

**Engine-freedom buys the tests.** Every §7.5 preflight sentence ("4 areas skipped: invalid geometry", "No usable areas in Zones", "The source layer has no features") is decided by counting `VectorPreflight.skipped` against `features.length`, in a pure unit test with no engine.

**Alternatives rejected.** `ST_Transform` exists in the wasm build, but §2 chose app-side reprojection and the design "does not depend on it"; using it would put the CRS answer in two places and make the offline story depend on whether `spatial` ships PROJ data. A second proj4 import inside `features/` would be a second door to a singleton-registry library the app deliberately dedupes (CLAUDE.md).

### (e) ONE Style-by-result seam: a descriptor on the definition, not a branch per tool

**Decision: `ToolDefinition.styleByResult: StyleByResult | null`. `RunFooter` reads the descriptor, picks the column with `pick(written)`, resolves the value (`median` / `mostFrequent` / a literal) and opens either a rule draft or the vector layer's Color by attribute. No `toolId` appears in `RunFooter`.**

M3 needs `solid_volume_m3 >` median (§7.2), `solid_valid = false` (§7.3), `extent_height_m >` median (§7.4), `roof_area_m2 >` median (§7.1), the first copied TEXT field `=` its most frequent value or `<prefix>matches_n > 0` (§7.5), `<prefix>distance_m <` median (§7.7), and a vector layer's Color by attribute on the first output column (§7.6). Five of the seven differ only in column, operator and value source; the sixth is a different surface. Written as branches in the footer that is a `switch` on `toolId` in a view component, which is exactly where a new tool gets forgotten.

**`pick` takes the written columns, not the prefix.** §6.2 says the draft's attribute is "the first column the run ACTUALLY wrote, in the order §7 lists for that tool (an unticked measure is never chosen)", and §7.5's is "the first copied TEXT field … if no text field was copied, on `<prefix>matches_n`" — a rule about the columns' TYPES, which is why Task 4's typed `outputColumns` must land first. The existing `run.columns[0]` (`RunFooter.tsx:241`) is `pick = (w) => w[0] ?? null` and stays the default for four tools.

**The boolean rule needs no editor change.** `ConditionOperator` includes `"="`, `Condition.value` is `number | string | boolean`, and `evaluateCondition` treats `"="` as a strict `===` (`navara-core` `dist/index.js:1194-1196`); `RulesEditor.tsx:755-774` already round-trips the literals `true`/`false` as booleans. Task 9 pins that with a test rather than assuming it.

**`median` must CAST to DOUBLE** (the M2 DECIMAL trap) and stays root-rows-only (`buildMedianSql`). `mostFrequent` is a new `sql.ts` builder over the same root-row restriction, for the same reason: a building with six parts must not outvote one with none.

### (f) A derived layer is prepared inside the run's own FIFO slot and published in one step

**Decision: `prepareDerivedCityLayer` mints the table name with `nextTableName()`, issues `CREATE TABLE <new> AS SELECT * FROM <parent table> WHERE COALESCE("feature_id","id") IN (<root ids>)`, writes the run's columns into it, builds the model copy, and returns a `DerivedPlan` whose `publish()` — called as the run's LAST step — calls `adoptLayerTable`, copies the parent's provenance entries into `useComputedColumnStore` under the new id, `addLayer({ …, insertAfterId: parent.id, derivedFrom })` and `activateLayer`. Nothing before `publish()` is visible; `discard()` drops everything.**

**The copy is cut from the parent's TABLE, not from the parent's source.** Re-reading a 300 MB CityJSON to produce a subset of rows the engine already holds is a minute of parsing for nothing, and it would need the reader — which the CityGML and CityParquet parents do not have, forcing a second code path for them. `CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT * FROM layer_N WHERE …` is ONE statement that works for every parent kind, brings the parent's own computed columns across WITH their values (§6's "inherited computed columns keep their provenance" — hence the provenance copy in `publish()`), and needs no geometry-column filtering because the browsing table never had geometry columns to begin with (`isDroppedColumn`, `columnKind.ts:74-80`).

**Reader-backedness is then METADATA plus a filter.** The derived `LayerTable` copies the parent's `source`, `reader`, `extension` and `lods` verbatim and sets `sourceFeatureIds` to the root ids it was cut with. That is what makes §6's promise true — "the reader re-reads the parent source filtered to those ids", so every tool, proxy and export format the parent supports works on the copy — and it is why `sourceFeatureIds` is a `LayerTable` field rather than a `deriveLayer` local: `readSource`'s reader `FROM`, `resolveScope`'s "all", and `buildCityParquetSourceSql`'s `where` are three independent readers of the parent's source on this layer's behalf, and every one of them must AND the filter in or a derived layer quietly reads the whole parent.

**`enqueueLayerTable` is unusable here and that is a hard fact, not a preference.** It goes through `enqueue` (`layerTables.ts:1200`), and the run is already inside a queued task — enqueueing from inside the queue is a deadlock. It would also break §6.1's cancel contract outright: "the results, the model copy, its table and the layer row are all prepared first and published together as the last step", and a fire-and-forget build (`addCityLayer.ts:154-164`) publishes the row immediately and the table whenever it gets to the front.

**Two new `layerTables` exports, both called only from inside a FIFO slot.** `nextTableName()` mints `` `layer_${++counter}` `` from the module's own counter, so a derived table can never collide with an ordinary build's name; `adoptLayerTable(layerId, info)` seeds the registry entry as `ready` so nothing rebuilds it. Both go into the 6 `vi.mock(".../insights/layerTables")` factories.

**The filter is over FEATURE roots, not rows.** `WHERE COALESCE("feature_id","id") IN (<root ids>)` — not `"id" IN (<row ids>)` — because §6's copy holds "the SCOPED features … with their geometry at every LoD", and a feature is its root plus its parts. The same root-id list becomes `sourceFeatureIds`.

**Three parent kinds, three answers.**

- **Reader-backed CityJSON/CityJSONSeq parent** — the copy keeps the parent's `source`, `reader`, `extension` and `lods`, plus `sourceFeatureIds` (§6, "What a derived layer is"; scenario 10's last clause).
- **CityGML / CityParquet parent** — the same CTAS, with `reader: null`, `source: null`, `lods: []` and `sourceFeatureIds` still set. Same limitations as the parent, which is what §6 asks for.
- **Streaming (FlatCityBuf) parent** — **a deviation.** `ResidentObjectRecord` (`workerProtocol.ts:51-73`) holds no boundaries at all, so the "static snapshot of the frozen features' resident records" §6 describes can carry attributes but no geometry: the layer would appear in the list, in the table and in Details, and render nothing. Building geometry from resident records means a worker-protocol change, which §9 lists as deferred ("Computing on layers without a reader"). **The plan's answer, ACCEPTED by the owner (Decisions recorded item 1): the New layer radio is DISABLED for a streaming target with a reason line** — **[adapted copy A2]** — and scenario 10's streaming variant is recorded as unmet at the gate. No task invents a worker change.

**Identity and independence.** `Layer.derivedFrom: { layerId, layerName, runId } | null` is a new field on every layer. It is NOT added to `App.tsx:1061-1078`'s explicit serialisation list, so it is not persisted by construction; the state line (`layerPresentation.ts:128-136`), the layer-list marker, the "Show run log" menu item and the snapshot filter all read it. §6.2's "independent of its parent from publication on" needs no mechanism — nothing links them — but `layerTableLifecycle.ts` must not treat a derived layer as a streaming rebuild candidate, and `installStaleWatcher` must not mark the run stale on the derived layer's own first table entry.

**Placement needs a store change.** `addLayer` appends (`layerStore.ts:347-349`) and there is no reorder; §6.2 wants the derived layer "inserted directly under its target in the layer list". `addLayer`'s input gains `insertAfterId?: string` and the push becomes a splice — one edit site, and every existing caller keeps append semantics.

**Cost if wrong:** two `layerTables` exports, one `Layer` field, one `addLayer` option.

### (g) The destination branch computes over the PARENT and writes into the COPY

**Decision: with `destination === "new"`, `execute` resolves the scope, reads the source and computes exactly as it does for "This layer" — same table, same ids, same executor — and then, instead of `writeComputedColumns` against the target's table, hands the `ToolResult` to `prepareDerivedCityLayer`/`prepareDerivedVectorLayer` and publishes. The target's table is never written.**

The executor must not know about the destination: §6's copy holds "the SCOPED features … all their existing attributes … and the new computed columns", which is the same rows the same compute produced. A second code path through the executors would be the place the two destinations silently diverge.

**The name is re-checked at publication, not only at Run** (§6, scenario 12). `disambiguate(name, layers, geoLayers)` appends `" (2)"` and reports `renamed: true`; the card then says so. Doing it at publication is what makes a queued run survive a rename in between, and it is inside the same FIFO slot as the publish, so nothing can take the name between the check and the `addLayer`.

**Undo removes the layer** (§6.2) and is blocked once the derived layer "has been the target or source of any later run (queued, running or done) and has no computed columns of its own"; renaming or restyling does not block it. `RunRecord.newLayerId` is what `undoRun` reads; the block is a scan of the run history for `targetLayerId === newLayerId || sourceLayerId === newLayerId` plus `computedColumnsOf(newLayerId).size > 0`. **The `removeLayer` call happens OUTSIDE the FIFO slot**, after `runOnTableQueue` resolves: `layerTableLifecycle`'s removal branch calls `dropLayerTable` (`:164`), which enqueues — removing from inside the slot would deadlock, exactly as `enqueueLayerTable` would.

**Four consequences the card and the row inherit.** `RunFooter`'s done card for a New-layer run reads `run.newLayerId ?? run.targetLayerId` for Open table, Style by result and Zoom to layer, so the actions point at the copy and not at the untouched target. The layer row's "Show run log" is disabled when `runById(derivedFrom.runId)` is null, because the history keeps only 20 runs (`processingStore.ts:22`) and a layer outlives its run. A vector TARGET whose `config.preparation !== "ready"` is refused — once, in `eligibility.ts`, beside the existing target-kind check, so the catalogue row and the Run button say the same thing. And `Layer.derivedFrom` is a REQUIRED field: Task 21 greps `tests/` for hand-built `Layer` literals and budgets the sweep in its own commit rather than making the field optional to dodge it.

### (h) Off-queue engine-death hardening is ONE change inside `duckdb.ts`

**Decision: `runQuery`, `ddl`, `queryDuckDB`, `registerBuffer`, `readFile` and `dropBuffer` race their in-flight await against `duckdb.ts`'s own death signal and return their ordinary failure value — `{ ok: false, message: "Analytics engine stopped" }`, `null`, `false`, `null`, and for `dropBuffer` simply return. No new export, no call-site edit, no mock-factory sweep.**

**`dropBuffer` is on the list for a reason that is easy to miss.** Its body is `await db.dropFile(name).catch(() => {})` (`duckdb.ts:740-745`), which swallows a REJECTION and does nothing about a promise that never settles — and `readSource.release()` and `VectorTableHandle.release()` both await it from a `finally` INSIDE the run's FIFO slot. A death during a cleanup would strand the queue for the life of the page, which is the exact failure `engineAwait.ts` exists for. `queryDuckDB` is included because its two legacy callers (`stacItems`, the old stats path) hang the same way and swallow-to-null is already their contract.

The hazard is precise: duckdb-wasm's `onError` clears its pending requests WITHOUT rejecting them, so a query caught by the death never settles (`engineAwait.ts:4-12`). `layerTables.ts:80-98` already solves it for itself by shadowing every primitive with a `racedWithDeath` wrapper — but `computedColumns.ts:20-27`, `export.ts:20` and every off-queue caller import the unraced originals, which is the M2 roadmap's "the export dialog and the counts never settle" and the parked "computedColumns' inner statement awaits are inert".

Putting the race in the primitive fixes all of them at once, and the six named callers (the export dialog and writer, the layer counts, the grid query, the map-filter sync, the Stats tab, `RunFooter`'s median) already handle `ok: false` — so they settle with a message instead of hanging, with zero edits. `duckdb.ts` owns `onEngineDeath` locally, so there is no import cycle with `engineAwait.ts` and no second copy of the race: the primitives race the SIGNAL, `engineAwait` races arbitrary promises, and `layerTables`'s wrappers keep working because the outer race still fires.

**The run queue's behaviour is unchanged, and provably so.** `markEngineDead` dispatches death listeners synchronously in registration order (`duckdb.ts:163-170`); in `raced(runQuery(sql), signal)` the inner listener is registered first and RESOLVES a promise (a microtask), while the outer listener REJECTS `raced`'s promise synchronously — so `EngineDeadError` still wins and a run still reads §6.1's "Analytics engine stopped" by the same path. Task 25 pins that ordering with a test rather than asserting it.

**The other three pieces of group D are separate and small:** `retryEngine` (`layerTables.ts:767-857`) captures `getEngineGeneration()` before `bootEngine()` and abandons if it moved; `undoRun`'s post-commit `EngineDeadError` catch (`runQueue.ts:971-977`) stops short-circuits before the model publication, the provenance rollback and the "Undone" card instead of falling through; `computedColumns.ts` needs no change at all once the primitive races, which is the cleanest possible answer to the M2 residual.

**Alternative rejected:** shadowing the primitives in `computedColumns.ts` and `export.ts` the way `layerTables.ts` does. It is the local precedent, but it is three copies of one idea and it leaves every FUTURE caller unprotected by default — the opposite of what a hazard with no visible symptom needs.

### (i) Palette rotation, and `Color by = Rules` at Save

**Decision: `RULE_PALETTE_HEX` in `src/scene/cityColors.ts` (beginning with `NEW_RULE_COLOR_HEX` so nothing about the first rule changes); `nextRuleColor(rules)` returns the first palette colour no enabled rule is already using, falling back to `RULE_PALETTE_HEX[index % length]`; both `defaultRuleFormValues()` and Style by result use it. `RunFooter` stops calling `updateLayer(layerId, { colorBy: "rules" })` when it opens the draft, and the rule editor's Save applies `ensureRulesMode()` — which it already does.**

Two bugs with one owner. Today every draft takes `#7cb518` (`RulesEditor.tsx:812`, `RunFooter.tsx:137`), so a second Style-by-result draft is invisible against the first; and `RunFooter.tsx:142` sets `colorBy` EAGERLY, so a layer on Surface type or Single colour repaints to the unmatched colour before the user has seen the draft — which contradicts §6.2's "The map does NOT change until the user presses Save in the editor, as with any rule". `ensureRulesMode` (`RulesEditor.tsx:158-165`) is the correct behaviour already written down; the fix is to let it be the only writer. Note it flips only from `"surface"`: a layer on `"single"` keeps its colour, which is the existing product decision and M3 does not change it.

**The palette must satisfy `cityColors.ts`'s collision rule** (no highlight, hover or base surface colour equal to a rule colour, pinned by `tests/unit/scene/cityColors.test.ts`). The eight `CATEGORY_PALETTE_HEX` values were chosen under the same constraint and are the obvious starting set, but they are the vector layers' categorical scale and reusing them verbatim would make a rule and a category read as the same thing. Task 26 pins a rule palette and extends the collision test. The list is settled (Decisions recorded item 3, **[adapted copy A9]**): `#7cb518` first, unchanged, then `#2563eb`, `#c2410c`, `#7e22ce`, `#0f766e`, `#be185d`, `#b45309`, `#15803d`.

**The third piece:** a run that went stale or was undone while its median was in flight still opens the draft (`RunFooter.tsx:101-144` checks the token and the layer's existence but not the run). The guard is one more re-read of the run record after the await, beside the existing `alive` check.

### (j) The streaming-table sweep compares versions

**Decision: `layerTableLifecycle.ts` keeps an `enqueuedVersions` map beside `knownVersions`, and `sweepStreamingLayers()` skips a layer whose current stream version equals the version at its last enqueued build.**

M2's final fix wave made the toolbox a table consumer, so opening Tools sweeps every streaming layer and rebuilds its table — which trips `installStaleWatcher` (`runQueue.ts:1153-1176`) on the `building → ready` transition and retires a finished card as "stale: layer reloaded" even though nothing about the data moved. The sweep's job is "a consumer opened and this layer's table is behind"; the version is exactly that question, and it is already the marker `residentModel.ts` documents for this purpose.

## Tasks

Execution order. One writer at a time; every shared seam lands before its consumers. Each task repeats its **Files**, **Interfaces**, **Intent** and **Commit** from the index that produced it, then the TDD steps.

### Task 1: The real-engine probes for `three_d` and `spatial`

**Files:**

- Create: `tests/integration/duckdb/solids.test.ts`, `tests/integration/duckdb/crossLayer.test.ts`, `fixtures/composite-solid.city.json` (Decisions recorded item 4), `fixtures/invalid-solid.city.json` (the commander's fixture ruling)
- Modify: `tests/integration/duckdb/harness.ts` (an installer beside the `cityjson` install in `openDuckDB`). `fixtures/README.md`'s rows for the two new fixtures are Task 28's.

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: `openDuckDB(): Promise<Harness>` and `fixtureBytes(fixture)` (`harness.ts:36, 88`).
- Produces: `export function installExtension(db: Harness, name: "spatial" | "three_d"): void` in `harness.ts`, and two `describe.skipIf(!enabled)` suites gated on `process.env.DUCKDB_INTEGRATION === "1"`.

**Why the SQL here is spelled LITERALLY and the builders are not imported.** `buildSolidMeasureSql` and `buildSolidValidationSql` do not exist yet — Task 6 creates them — so this suite cannot issue them. The rejection criterion "re-spelling SQL a later task will build" is satisfied in TWO places, and both are named so no reviewer has to guess: the literal below is copied VERBATIM into Task 6's unit test as the expected output of `buildSolidMeasureSql`, and Task 6 appends one case to `solids.test.ts` that runs the builder's own output against this engine. From Task 6 onwards the literal and the builder are pinned to each other; until then the literal is the only statement of the fact.

**This suite is opt-in and offline-safe.** It matches `tests/**/*.test.ts`, so the default run COLLECTS it and `describe.skipIf` keeps it from executing. The harness is imported DYNAMICALLY inside `beforeAll`, exactly as `layerTables.test.ts:128` does it, because a top-level import would evaluate the node bindings in every offline run.

**What this task pins and what it does NOT.** It pins the ENGINE's behaviour, spelled literally, for both extensions. It does not pin any builder's TEXT: `buildSolidMeasureSql` / `buildSolidValidationSql` (Task 6), `buildVectorTableSql` (Task 13), `buildFeatureProxySql` (Task 14) and `buildAggregateSql` (Task 19) are each pinned by their OWN task, which appends a case running that builder's output against this same engine — Task 6 to `solids.test.ts`, Tasks 13, 14, 16 and 19 to `crossLayer.test.ts` — Task 16's append is the three PREDICATES (`ST_CoveredBy` vs `ST_Within`, a boundary centre, a degenerate `ST_MakeEnvelope`), which a unit test over a fake `query` cannot see. (Task 17 appends nothing: its statement is `buildFeatureProxySql` joined to the vector table, and both halves are already pinned.) No later task may say "Task 1 already covers it": Task 1 covers the FACT, the owning task covers the TEXT.

**This task also adds TWO fixtures, both spelled out in full in Step 1.**

`fixtures/composite-solid.city.json` (Decisions recorded item 4) is a minimal CityJSON 2.0 file with one Building whose LoD `"2.2"` geometry is a `CompositeSolid` of two unit cubes sharing a face — local `(0,0,0)`-`(1,1,1)` and `(1,0,0)`-`(2,1,1)` over the RD translate, so the members' volumes sum to exactly 2. Every ring is wound counter-clockwise seen from OUTSIDE (each member's signed volume is `+1`, checked by the divergence formula before this plan was written), because an unoriented fixture makes `ST_3DVolume` RAISE — the very trap this plan's guard exists for.

`fixtures/invalid-solid.city.json` (the commander's fixture ruling) is one Building with **no parts** whose LoD `"2.2"` `Solid` is NOT closed: it is `NL.IMBAG.Pand.0001`'s own solid from `two-buildings.city.json`, lifted out with the nine vertices it uses — 7 faces, 2 open edges, 1 non-manifold edge, `is_valid` false, `is_closed` false, envelope 388 m², footprint 80 m², zmin 0, zmax 8.4. It exists because `two-buildings.city.json` cannot express "a building whose solid is invalid" at the FEATURE level: `NL.IMBAG.Pand.0001` has a MultiSurface PART at 2.2, so §7's contributor rule makes the PART the contributor and the whole feature reads "not a solid". Over `two-buildings`, Measure solids therefore measures ONE feature (`NL.IMBAG.Pand.0002`, valid, volume 2178) and skips one ("not a solid"); every FEATURE-level "invalid solid" expectation in this milestone uses `invalid-solid.city.json` instead.

Both rows go into `fixtures/README.md` (Task 28).

```

The nesting is CityJSON 2.0's: a `CompositeSolid`'s boundaries are an array of SOLIDS, each solid an array of SHELLS, each shell an array of SURFACES, each surface an array of RINGS. The two solids share the face `x = 1` (vertices 1, 2, 6, 5), which is why this is a composite and not a MultiSolid of two disjoint boxes. No `semantics` block: semantics are optional and nothing here reads them — the parser test for `geometryType` is Task 2's, on hand-built models.
